name: Kamal
description: Protects against destructive Kamal 2.x operations that tear down the stack, \ delete accessory data directories, drop proxy routing, take the app offline, \ or prune the images that rollback depends on.

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-remove
destructive_patterns.description: kamal remove tears down the entire deployment, including stateful accessories.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal remove` removes the app container, kamal-proxy, and all accessory containers \ from the servers and logs out of the registry. Because it removes accessories, it can \ destroy stateful services (Postgres/Redis/search) along with the rest of the stack. \ It accepts `-y`/`--yes` to skip the confirmation prompt, so a non-interactive agent \ run has no safety net. A wrong destination (e.g. a missing `-d staging` while the \ shell points at production) tears down prod.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal details: review what is actually deployed first \ - kamal app remove / kamal proxy remove: scope the teardown if that is the real intent \ - Always pass the explicit destination (e.g. -d staging) and confirm it

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-accessory-remove
destructive_patterns.description: kamal accessory remove deletes the accessory container, image, AND its host data directory.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal accessory remove [NAME]` removes the accessory container and image and ALSO \ deletes its data directory from the host. For a database/redis/search accessory this \ permanently destroys the data. `kamal accessory remove all` does this across every \ accessory at once (highest blast radius). The common mistake is meaning the YAML block \ in deploy.yml, not the live Postgres/Redis data on disk.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Edit the accessory block out of deploy.yml instead of deleting live data \ - kamal accessory stop: take it offline reversibly (data preserved) \ - Back up the data directory / take a database dump before any removal

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-app-remove
destructive_patterns.description: kamal app remove takes the app offline by removing its containers and images.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal app remove` removes the app containers and images from the servers. The app goes \ offline and the images must be rebuilt or re-pulled before it can serve again. This is \ a frequent footgun when asked to "clean up old containers".

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal app stale_containers: list leftover containers without removing the live app \ - kamal prune: remove genuinely old images/containers (still erodes rollback) \ - kamal app maintenance: serve a 503 reversibly instead of removing

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-app-stop
destructive_patterns.description: kamal app stop stops the app container, causing an outage until restarted.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal app stop` stops the app container on the servers, causing an outage until \ `kamal app start`. There is no built-in confirmation prompt.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal app maintenance: serve a 503 maintenance page (reversible with kamal app live) \ - kamal app details: confirm the target before stopping anything

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-proxy-remove
destructive_patterns.description: kamal proxy remove drops routing for every app behind that proxy on the host.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal proxy remove` removes the kamal-proxy container and image. Every app behind that \ proxy on the host loses routing until the proxy is re-booted. There is no confirmation \ prompt for `remove`.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal proxy details / kamal proxy logs: diagnose the proxy without removing it \ - kamal proxy reboot --rolling: if a cycle is required, stagger it to limit the outage

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-proxy-reboot
destructive_patterns.description: kamal proxy reboot stops, removes, and recreates the proxy, causing a short outage.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal proxy reboot` stops, removes, and starts a new proxy container. It is documented \ to cause a small outage on each server. While it prompts interactively, a non-interactive \ agent run with `-y` skips that prompt.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal proxy reboot --rolling: stagger the restart across servers to reduce the outage \ - kamal proxy restart: a lighter restart of the existing proxy where applicable

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-proxy-stop
destructive_patterns.description: kamal proxy stop drops routing for every app behind that proxy until it is started.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal proxy stop` stops the kamal-proxy container. Every app behind that proxy on the \ host loses routing until `kamal proxy start`/`boot`.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal proxy details: confirm what the proxy is serving before stopping it \ - kamal proxy restart: cycle the proxy without leaving it down

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-accessory-reboot
destructive_patterns.description: kamal accessory reboot stops, removes, and recreates the accessory container (downtime).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal accessory reboot [NAME]` stops, removes, and starts a new accessory container, \ causing downtime for that accessory (e.g. the database). Data survives only if a volume \ is mapped; an unmapped data directory is at risk. `NAME=all` reboots every accessory.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal accessory restart: restart the existing container without remove/recreate \ - kamal accessory details: confirm the target accessory before cycling it

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-accessory-stop
destructive_patterns.description: kamal accessory stop stops the accessory (e.g. the database), erroring the app.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal accessory stop [NAME]` stops the accessory container. Stopping the database (or \ cache/search) errors the app until the accessory is restarted, knocking a dependency \ offline mid-traffic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal accessory restart: cycle it without leaving it stopped \ - kamal accessory details / kamal accessory logs: diagnose without stopping

destructive_patterns.name: kamal-prune
destructive_patterns.description: kamal prune removes older images/containers that kamal rollback relies on.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`kamal prune all` prunes unused images and stopped containers, `kamal prune containers` \ prunes stopped containers except the last n (default 5), and `kamal prune images` prunes \ unused images. Kamal's `rollback` relies on the older deployed images/containers, so \ over-pruning can strand a deployment with no rollback target.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kamal app containers / kamal app images: see what would be removed first \ - Confirm a known-good rollback target exists before pruning
